correctness.rationale: The zero-letter branch follows from reflexivity and syntax induction. The one-agent classwise support lemma eliminates one of at most 2^k Boolean types at each strict step, simultaneously bounding arbitrarily many (even infinite) equivalence classes; a maximum-type formula attains the bound. Alternating 2-element equivalence blocks on n points force the fixed depth-one one-letter formula to delete one terminal point each round. Empty terminal handling, quantifiers, k=0, and extra agents are covered. Independent checker replay 3016 finite cases supports but is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact sharp resource frontier for a standard epistemic update operation: the one-agent horizon depends only on the number of factual letters, even for infinite state sets, while the jump to two agents destroys any uniform bound already for a fixed one-letter depth-one formula. The quantitative classification is meaningful independently of numerical experiments and does not require a downstream theorem.
